paper.title: Lunar laser ranging analyses of NGLR-1 data with PEP and prospects for MPAc: towards one millimeter range precision
paper.abstract: Since 1969, Lunar Laser Ranging (LLR) has provided critical data for investigating Earth-Moon dynamics, lunar internal structure, and tests of General Relativity (GR). However, the measurement precision of historical arrays (such as those from Apollo and Lunokhod missions) is inherently limited by laser pulse broadening induced by lunar librations. To overcome this limit, next-generation single Cube Corner Retroreflectors (CCRs) of large optical diameter have been developed to eliminate pulse dispersion, enabling LLR measurements to advance from centimeter-level precision down to the millimeter scale. In this work, we present a detailed analysis of LLR observations from NGLR-1 (Next Generation Lunar Retroreflector-1), the first single 10cm-diameter CCR deployed on the lunar surface. Carried out using the Planetary Ephemeris Program (PEP), this study investigates individual range measurements, normal points (NPs), residuals, and observational dispersion collected by the ground stations at Apache Point Observatory Lunar laser ranging station (APOL), Wettzell, and Grasse. The results: demonstrate the success of NGLR-1 in significantly enhancing time of flight measurement precision compared to legacy Apollo and Lunokhod retroreflector arrays; indicate similar good prospects also for ESA's MPAc laser retroreflector (MoonLIGHT with Pointing Actuators) to be launched in early 2027; pave the way for a new era of LLR observations and enhanced tests of GR, alternative gravity theories in general and improved lunar geophysics and geodesy.

paper.title: Orbital dynamics and gravitational wave of Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole immersed in perfect fluid dark matter
paper.abstract: The dynamical properties of bound particle orbits around a Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole immersed in perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM) are investigated. An analysis of the horizon topology shows that both event and cosmological horizons emerge within specific parametric regimes. Curvature invariants, including the Ricci scalar, Ricci-squared, and Kretschmann scalar, confirm the existence of a curvature singularity at $r = 0$. By utilizing the pericenter precession data of the S2 star in Sgr A*, the PFDM parameter is constrained to $0 < λ< 7.726412 \times 10^{5}$ M$_{\odot}$. For a source moving along a periodic orbit, the emitted gravitational waveforms exhibit two key features: (i) the orbital period increases with the ``zoom'' number, accompanied by a modest growth in wave amplitude, and (ii) the PFDM parameter nonlinearly modulates the period, leading to a slight amplitude suppression and introducing only a negligible phase shift relative to the vacuum case. These results explicitly characterize the local imprints of PFDM on relativistic orbital dynamics and offer predictions that are testable by future high-precision astrometric and gravitational-wave observations.

paper.title: Gyromagnetic ratios of slowly rotating charged Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes
paper.abstract: Charged Ellis--Bronnikov wormholes, supported by a phantom scalar field in Einstein--Maxwell theory, connect two asymptotically flat regions, so a rotating member carries a magnetic dipole moment and a gyromagnetic ratio at each mouth. We construct the slowly rotating family in closed form on all three background branches and show that, within the stationary axial dipole sector and with no applied magnetic field, the first-order solution is unique. The two gyromagnetic ratios obey an exact deficit relation set by the static geometry alone. It gives $g_\pm<2$ at both mouths, bounds the deficit by two-thirds of the squared ratio of scalar to electric charge, and, through the positivity of the reduced magnetic moment, gives each ratio the sign of the mass of its own mouth; the two ratios coincide only for reflection-symmetric throats, so their difference measures the asymmetry of the wormhole. Rotation drags the two ends relative to each other in a definite sense, with a dragging profile that decreases monotonically across the throat, and the electromagnetic field carries a strictly positive share of the angular momentum on every finite sphere. Toward the extremal edge at the positive mouth the deficit closes cubically on every trajectory studied, because the redshift factor at the throat vanishes quadratically; the coefficient depends on the path. When the charge is switched off, the frame dragging reproduces known neutral results, whereas on the massive neutral branch the gyromagnetic ratios stay away from the Kerr--Newman value.

paper.title: Testing the Universality of RAR Model with Constraints on Fermionic Dark Matter for M31
paper.abstract: The Ruffini--Argüelles--Rueda (RAR) model describes dark matter as a self-gravitating system of massive fermions in thermodynamic equilibrium within general relativity. It suggests a dual morphology in galaxies: a highly degenerate quantum core mimicking a central supermassive black hole, and a classical halo that explains galactic rotation curves. Earlier applications of the model to the Milky Way restricted the fermion mass to $mc^{2}=48\text{--}345~\text{keV}$, and the orbits of the S-stars around Sagittarius~A$^{\ast}$ (Sgr~A$^{\ast}$) favored $mc^{2}=56~\text{keV}$, whereas a recent thermodynamic stability analysis allows only $mc^{2}\approx194\text{--}387~\text{keV}$. In this work, we apply the RAR model to the Andromeda galaxy (M31), which hosts a dark compact object of approximately $1.4\times10^{8}~M_{\odot}$ within $0.19~\text{pc}$, roughly 33 times the mass of Sgr~A$^{\ast}$. We solve the relativistic equilibrium equations for $mc^{2}=6\text{--}60~\text{keV}$. For all these masses, the fermionic core lies within $0.19~\text{pc}$ and provides the central mass without a black hole. With a bulge and disk added, the total rotation curve is statistically acceptable ($χ^{2}/N_{\text{dof}}\approx1.18$) but lies below the disk data at $3\text{--}11~\text{kpc}$, an offset attributed to the baryonic models we adopted. The Navarro--Frenk--White (NFW) and Burkert profiles fitted to the same data give a lower $χ^{2}$ but require an additional black hole. The stability of the M31 core against gravitational collapse limits the fermion mass to $mc^{2}\lesssim60~\text{keV}$. With the earlier Milky Way range, a single fermion can therefore describe both galaxies only for $mc^{2}=48\text{--}60~\text{keV}$, which includes $56~\text{keV}$. With the thermodynamic range, no fermionic core can supply the central mass of M31, so M31 would have to host a black hole.

paper.title: The OGLE Collection of Variable Stars. Over 1.3 Million Human-Verified Eclipsing and Ellipsoidal Binaries in the Milky Way
paper.abstract: We present a new release of the OGLE collection of eclipsing and ellipsoidal binary systems in the Galactic bulge and disk. The catalog contains 1 330 024 objects, including 1 280 765 eclipsing binaries and 49 259 ellipsoidal variables, nearly three times as many systems as the previous editions of the OGLE collection. The selection and classification process involved expert visual inspection of the light curves. The catalog incorporates all available OGLE-II, OGLE-III, and OGLE-IV photometry, extending the observational baseline to nearly 28 years for some objects. paper.title: Actionless Branes on Axion Wormholes
paper.abstract: Can a Euclidean axion wormhole extend to infinity with every instanton still suppressed? The imaginary distance bound says it cannot: some instanton must become actionless first. Calabi-Yau compactifications appear to violate the bound: several axions share the field excursion, and the instantons charged under any one of them stay suppressed all the way. We show that the wormhole can hide from these instantons but not from their bound states: misaligned central charges make a bound state cheaper than its constituents, while the axions act on every constituent. On the type IIB wormhole supported by two axions of the Neveu-Schwarz two-form, a fivebrane carrying string charge becomes actionless at large volume within two thirds of the way to infinity, for either relative sign of the axions and however they share the excursion. In S-dual variables it is a D5-brane with magnetic flux for one sign and a D5-NS5 bound state for the other. Adding more axions does not help: the same branes become actionless on every Calabi-Yau threefold, because what counts is the degree of homogeneity of the saxion sector, not the number of axions. These bound states are what the convex-hull axion weak gravity conjecture requires.

paper.title: Dirac leptogenesis with charged leptons
paper.abstract: Popular frameworks that explain the baryon asymmetry of the Universe (BAU) are electroweak baryogenesis, requiring a first-order phase transition, and Majorana leptogenesis, which relies on lepton number violation in the neutrino sector. Dirac leptogenesis offers an alternative mechanism that avoids both requirements, instead allowing the BAU to follow from previously generated chiral asymmetries that remain out of equilibrium in the early Universe. Conventional realizations of this scenario typically invoke ultra-light Dirac neutrinos. In this work, we generalize the mechanism to include Standard Model charged leptons by assuming that their mass-generating interactions have a UV origin and arise from higher-dimensional operators. For concreteness, the analysis is performed within a Froggatt-Nielsen setup, which allows us to naturally address fermionic mass hierarchies, too, now linked to the BAU, and we show that the proposed mechanism is viable by supercooling the flavon phase transition. The framework predicts a flavon with a (1.7-50) GeV mass, bounded by the non-observation of lepton flavor violation and the requirement for the Universe to not reheat above sphaleron temperatures, which could be indirectly probed by future lepton flavor violation experiments.

paper.title: Numerical Implementation and Tests of the Quadratic Effective Action for Lorentzian Spinfoam Amplitudes
paper.abstract: In the pure integral representation of Lorentzian EPRL spinfoam amplitudes, the integration over non-geometric variables in the large-spin limit defines an effective action for Regge geometries. Expanding this effective action to quadratic order around a flat background recovers the classical Regge action $iS_{\mathrm{Regge}}$ at leading order, supplemented by a curvature correction quadratic in the bulk deficit angles $\varepsilon$. In this work, we numerically implement this effective-action framework and validate its analytic predictions using two Julia packages: LorentzianSimplexSolver, for the computation of real and complex critical-point data, and Effective-Spinfoam, for the evaluation of the effective action. We apply this workflow to the double-$Δ_3$ complex, the $1$-$5$ Pachner move, its refinement, and a $24$-simplex hypercube triangulation. Two complementary numerical tests are performed: first, starting from the real critical point of a flat background, we verify that the leading term reproduces the quadratic Regge action and evaluate the $\varepsilon^2$ curvature correction across a range of the Barbero-Immirzi parameter $γ$. Power-law fits confirm that in the small-$γ$ regime, the $\varepsilon^2$ correction is of higher order in $γ$ than the Regge action. Second, for a sample of curved geometries with finite length perturbations $δ\ell$, we numerically solve the full nonlinear critical equations at fixed perturbed edge lengths for complex critical points. By comparing the direct action evaluation at complex critical points with the quadratic effective action, we demonstrate that the latter accurately reproduces the nonlinear complex critical-point action up to remainders of cubic order in $δ\ell$.

paper.title: Pure integral formula of spinfoam amplitude and curvature corrections in effective theory
paper.abstract: We develop a new analytic method for the semiclassical analysis of the Lorentzian EPRL spinfoam amplitude on a fixed triangulation. We derive a pure integral formula for the spinfoam amplitude that trades the discrete sum over internal spins for integrals over continuous variables. This reformulation is free of discrete sums and provides a well-behaved action that is well-adapted to the stationary phase approximation in the large-spin regime. Integrating out the non-geometric variables yields an effective action for the edge lengths of the Regge geometry. Applying the stationary phase approximation and expanding this effective action to second order in perturbations around a flat background, we obtain the classical Regge action at leading order, supplemented by a quadratic correction in the deficit angles $\varepsilon$. This curvature correction originates from two distinct sources: a holonomy correction resulting from the new action and the fluctuations of non-Regge areas. We show that the quadratic $\varepsilon$ correction appears at a higher order in the Barbero-Immirzi parameter $γ$ relative to the Regge action. Together with the large-spin expansion, this yields a two-parameter expansion for the spinfoam effective action, whose leading order is the quadratic Regge action. In the long wavelength regime, the latter approaches the action of a massless spin-2 graviton.

paper.title: Simulation-based inference for gravitational-wave cosmology: parameter reconstruction of a first-order electroweak phase transition
paper.abstract: The detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) from a cosmological first- order phase transition would be unambiguous evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model, with a strong electroweak phase transition (EWPT) at LISA as a prime example. Reconstructing the underlying model from such a signal is challenging, since the map from the model parameters to the spectrum is degenerate and strong transitions occupy only small and sparse regions of parameter space. We show that simulation-based inference (SBI), a likelihood-free approach applicable to generic SGWB sources, provides a reliable parameter reconstruction despite these difficulties. We first apply SBI to the thermodynamic parameters characterizing the transition, namely its strength, inverse duration, temperature and bubble wall velocity. As a concrete application, we then consider a strong EWPT in a singlet extension of the Standard Model and reconstruct the model parameters from the resulting SGWB. We find that the SBI posteriors agree with those of a likelihood-based Markov chain Monte Carlo analysis, at negligible cost per data set once the network has been trained. Using the network posterior as the proposal for importance sampling with the exact likelihood further corrects its remaining deviations, at a sampling efficiency several orders of magnitude higher than sampling from the prior. SBI thus offers a fast and flexible framework for the cosmological science case of LISA

paper.title: Subsolar neutron star-black hole binaries from collapsars: Gravitational waveform models and detectability in current searches
paper.abstract: Detecting subsolar objects in binary mergers would be an exceptional discovery in gravitational wave astronomy. So far, dedicated searches for subsolar coalescences reported no confident detections, setting upper bounds on their merger rate. Given that standard stellar evolution is not able to produce subsolar candidates, a confident detection would point either to new physics or to unconventional astrophysical pathways. These include collapsars, where the outer parts of neutrino-cooled accretion disks around newborn stellar-mass black holes are subject to fragmentation and give rise to subsolar neutron stars, which can later merge with the central black hole. We show that current subsolar searches may miss a significant fraction of these neutron star-black hole mergers, because their templates do not account for the small mass ratios, the tidal disruption of the neutron star, and the effects of the surrounding gas. This result motivates improving the waveform modeling used in current subsolar searches and building adequate template banks tailored to these systems.

paper.title: Entanglement entropy from fundamental strings
paper.abstract: In previous work, we derived the local entropy capacity from off-shell string theory and combined it with the gravitational replica construction and flow-cut duality to normalize the entropy flow carried by physical fundamental strings. In this paper, we apply this framework to interval entanglement in holographic CFT$_2$. We construct explicit on-shell F1 worldsheets in the AdS$_3$ vacuum and planar BTZ, derive their Kalb-Ramond source currents, and show that the normalized spatial currents saturate the corresponding RT surface. Their flux reproduces both the vacuum single interval entropy and the finite temperature CFT$_2$ result. We then vary the NS-NS flux fraction. Although the total maximal flux remains unchanged, the F1 equations continuously redistribute the strings among different parts of the complement. In planar BTZ, the resulting signed flux through the bifurcation line reproduces the extensive thermal entropy and can vanish in the pure NS-NS limit without changing the interval entropy. Thus the on-shell string dynamics additionally determines its physical routing and boundary contact structure.

paper.title: EuclidFM: Foundation Model for Compact Photometric Survey Representation
paper.abstract: We present EuclidFM, a compact self-supervised model that learns object-level representations from heterogeneous catalogue photometry in Euclid Quick Data Release 1. Using 90,258 sources across three Euclid Deep Fields, a masked-autoencoder Transformer reconstructs withheld fluxes and uncertainties from available measurements, producing a 128-dimensional embedding per source. The embeddings encode morphological and photometric information: sources with high point-like probability have, on average, 12.4 similarly classified neighbours among their 15 nearest neighbours, compared with 4.3 under field- and magnitude-stratified randomization. Linear models trained on frozen embeddings predict VIS magnitudes with correlations of 0.954-0.980 across three held-out fields. For sources with VIS aperture-flux uncertainties up to 1 microJy, incorporating embeddings reduces the root-mean-square error in predicted log uncertainty by at least 24% relative to a magnitude-only model. A classifier trained on spectroscopically confirmed sources identifies 1,150 quasar candidates, but only 21 of the 156 candidates with accepted external counterparts show AGN evidence, including 12 spectroscopic quasars. The classifier's transferability to the wider photometric catalogue therefore remains uncertain, and its purity and completeness require further evaluation. Independently of classification, EuclidFM provides a common representation for downstream survey analyses when photometric coverage differs between sources. Code and data are available at https://github.com/AI-Driven-HEP/EuclidFM.

paper.title: Soft Factorisation of WQFT and the Spinning 4PM Magnusian
paper.abstract: We derive the soft divergences of $\hat{N}=-i\log\hat{S}$ in the Worldline Quantum Field Theory (WQFT) formalism, focusing on poles due to single massive-massive (Coulomb) and massive-massless (tail) graviton exchanges. Our derivation is inspired by the Faddeev-Kulish procedure, switching the interaction picture to one with an infrared-finite $\hat{N}$-matrix. Soft divergences emerging from the worldline are correlators of Wilson lines. As confirmation of this structure, we demonstrate explicitly how divergences of inclusive observables including the momentum impulse $Δp_i^μ$ and spin kick $ΔS_i^μ$ cancel, and we reproduce the infrared divergence of the one-loop scattering waveform. Using the Magnus series representation of $\hat{N}$ and Murua coefficients, we then calculate the Magnusian $N=\langle0|\hat{N}|0\rangle$ at fourth post-Minkowskian (4PM) order, including linear-in-spin corrections. For aligned spins, $-\partial N/\partial L$ reproduces the full scattering angle through 3PM order; at 4PM order, $N$ develops a soft divergence as predicted by our soft factorisation. Using the Feynman $i0^+$ prescription, we also derive an infrared-finite 4PM Magnusian which compactly encodes existing results for the conservative momentum impulse and spin kick via nested iterations of Poisson brackets.

paper.title: Spiral Pitch Angles in Black Hole Images and Movies
paper.abstract: The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) has produced images of M87* and Sgr A*, and will soon produce time sequences of images, or movies. General relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (GRMHD) models predict EHT sources will exhibit brightness fluctuations along the ring. The fluctuations are commonly connected to trailing spiral features. Here, we introduce a method to measure the pitch angle $ψ$ of radially extended features by cross-correlating brightness fluctuations sampled on rings at two distinct impact parameters. Pitch angle can be reliably measured from synthetic movies with BHEX resolution, and can be constrained even at EHT resolution. Single images enable noisy constraints of $ψ$. Pitch angle depends most on the viewing inclination and black hole spin. For constant inclination, the spiral winding direction depends on the sign of spin, with spirals winding more tightly in the direction of frame dragging near the horizon. The pitch angle will complement other observables to reliably constrain both the source inclination and spin in future analysis by EHT, and by expansions to the EHT such as ngEHT and BHEX.

paper.title: Revealing galaxy assembly bias with luminosity-weighted marked correlations
paper.abstract: We investigate whether luminosity-weighted marked correlation functions can reveal secondary halo information beyond that encoded by halo mass alone, as expected in scenarios of galaxy assembly bias. We propose a controlled null test in which galaxy luminosities follow the same mean luminosity--halo mass relation and scatter, while their residuals are either (A) uncorrelated with secondary halo properties or (B) correlated with a standardized secondary halo property, $s$. Both models have identical halo occupation, galaxy positions, luminosity function, and unweighted projected two-point correlation function, $w_p(r_p)$, so their distinction is encoded entirely in the luminosity marks. At leading order, the projected marked correlation function difference, $Δ\mathcal{M}_p(r_p)$, scales as $ρ^2σ_{\log L}^2ξ_{ss}(r_p)$, where $ρ$ controls the coupling between the luminosity and secondary-property residuals, $σ_{\log L}$ is the scatter in log luminosity at fixed halo mass, and $ξ_{ss}$ describes the spatial correlation of the secondary property. We test this framework using a DESI-BGS mock catalogue over $0.1<z<0.4$. For the injected dependence, we detect a marked-clustering deviation over $0.11<r_p/(h^{-1}\,{\rm Mpc})<1.04$, obtaining $χ^2=30.14$ relative to the null covariance. A one-parameter test rejects the mass-only hypothesis at greater than $5σ$ significance ($p=2.13\times10^{-7}$) for $|ρ|>0.63$. At fixed $σ_{\log L}=0.23$, correlations as weak as $|ρ|\simeq0.52$ remain detectable, with the results stable under variations in the HOD prescription and modelled galaxy selection effects. These results establish luminosity-weighted marked clustering as a sensitive null test for property-based galaxy assembly bias and secondary halo information hidden from unweighted two-point clustering.

paper.title: On the High Eccentricity Orbit of 51 Eri b and Constraints on Interactions with a Second Companion
paper.abstract: The eccentricity of an exoplanet's orbit is a key observational quantity that can be used to infer its dynamical past and predict its future orbital evolution. Planets are expected to emerge from their protoplanetary cradles with roughly circular eccentricities, and non-circular eccentricites to arise from subsequent dynamical processing in the absence of the gas disk. We present an updated orbit for 51 Eridani b based on 5 years of 0.2 mas precision optical interferometry from VLTI/GRAVITY(+). This planet is young (${\sim}20\,\mathrm{Myr}$ old), temperate ($T_{\rm eff}\sim650\,\mathrm{K}$), and on a wide orbit ($a{=}9.36\,\mathrm{au}$) with an uncertain mass ($M_{\rm b}\leq12\,M_{\rm J}$). We measured the planet's motion to an exceptionally high precision, confirming that its orbit is very eccentric ($e_b=0.574\pm0.003$). We observe residuals to the absolute astrometry of the host star based on a single planet orbit that could be attributable to reflex motion from a third body in the system. We construct a two companion orbit model that could explain the apparent reflex motion of 51 Eri A: this model predicts that the putative second companion has $M_c\in[1.0, 2900]_{95\%}\,M_{\rm Jup}$ and $a_c\in[0.3, 3.1]_{95\%}\,\mathrm{au}$. In this framework, a dynamical interaction between b and ``c" could have kicked the exterior, lower mass b out onto its present, eccentric orbit. If this signal is astrophysical, and not due to a systematic error, this candidate should be confirmable with Gaia DR4 epoch astrometry in the near future.

paper.title: Intra-day variability of the gamma-ray/optical emission of 3C 454.3: the complexity beyond the long-term correlation
paper.abstract: Simultaneous $γ$-ray/optical observations probe particle acceleration and radiative processes in blazar jets. The blazar 3C 454.3 shows a significant long-term correlation between these bands, often interpreted as support for the canonical one-zone leptonic emission model. However, both bands show strong intra-day variability, and whether the correlation persists during individual flares remains unclear.   We study the $γ$-ray/optical correlation and intra-day variability of 3C 454.3 over 17 years (2007--2024), on timescales $\leq 24$ h.   We analyse AGILE and Fermi-LAT observations using light curves binned from 3 to 48 h, together with simultaneous $R$-band photometry from WEBT and public optical data sets. We examine the flux and spectral evolution of individual flares, estimate time-dependent correlation properties, and derive Compton dominance from optical and $γ$-ray luminosities.   We confirm the long-term correlation, but find large intrinsic dispersion and a slope of $η\simeq 1.6$--$1.7$, inconsistent with a single canonical one-zone scenario. On shorter timescales, correlation strengths range from weak to strong, with slopes spanning $η\simeq 0.4$--$2.0$. We also find orphan flares in both bands, diverse flare morphologies, distinct Compton-dominance patterns with rapid excursions from $\sim 10$ to 120, and heterogeneous spectral trends. The shortest resolved variability timescales ($t_{\rm var} \lesssim 3$ h) indicate that localized emission regions are required by causality.   The $γ$-ray/optical correlation in 3C 454.3 thus arises not from a single emission regime, but from multiple epoch-dependent physical states. Increasing temporal resolution reveals richer variability, highlighting the importance of systematic intra-day, multi-epoch studies of bright FSRQs.

paper.title: Strong Coupling of Cosmological Perturbations in mLQC-I: The Hybrid Approach
paper.abstract: We study nonlinear perturbative consistency of scalar perturbations in modified loop quantum cosmology I (mLQC-I) within the hybrid approach. We express the quadratic and cubic Hamiltonians in a common canonical representation before imposing the background constraint and adopt a minimal sector-preserving cubic regularization. Near the pre-bounce quantum-geometrical de Sitter phase, nonlinear coefficients become strongly enhanced. The $α_I^3/κ$ term survives the leading ultraviolet cubic kernel for fixed nondegenerate triangles in the selected frequency assignment. This enhancement occurs in four inflationary potentials, with formal suppression scales sensitive to their normalization. In an assumed factorized quartic continuation, a selected lapse contact does not cancel enhanced cubic exchange in an analytic scattering family. However, the derived quartic Legendre contribution cancels that lapse contact at $V=K_φ$ in the Hamiltonian. The full amplitude remains unresolved: omitted quartic sectors are not proved subleading, and the formal scales do not determine a physical cutoff. paper.title: Where Did the Angular Momentum Go? WASP-12 b May Have Circularized on a Retrograde Orbit
paper.abstract: WASP-12 b is the only exoplanet with confirmed orbital decay. Angular momentum transferred from its decaying orbit should have realigned the star's thin convective layer, yet an earlier Rossiter--McLaughlin (RM) measurement suggested a $\sim$60$^\circ$ spin--orbit misalignment. We present two new Keck Planet Finder RM measurements. We measure a sky-projected obliquity of $λ=-1.3\pm8.7^\circ$; and the star's projected rotation velocity is $v\sin i_\star=1.3\pm0.1~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, an order of magnitude lower than expected for a star of its mass and age. With WASP-12's low chromospheric activity, $\log R^\prime_{\rm HK}=-5.5$, our analysis favors an aligned system in which $v\sin i_\star$ reflects slow surface rotation with $P_{\rm rot}\sim60$ days, rather than a projection effect. Our evolution models favor a late-main-sequence star rather than a subgiant, with a central convective core found in 99\% of posterior samples. This internal structure suppresses the central-focusing and nonlinear wave-breaking mechanisms for inward-propagating gravity waves. We propose that WASP-12 b was initially placed on a retrograde orbit after high-eccentricity migration, when its host rotated at $v\sin i_\star\approx14$~km~s$^{-1}$ (or $P_{\rm rot}\sim$6 days). Tidal decay transferred orbital angular momentum to the convective envelope, aligning the surface. The retrograde interior acts as an angular-momentum reservoir, while interior--envelope coupling slows the surface rotation. A semi-empirical relation gives an envelope--interior angular-momentum exchange timescale of $\sim4$~Myr, similar to the observed orbital-decay timescale of $\sim3.25$~Myr. The angular-momentum budget also permits this initially retrograde evolution. In contrast, an initially prograde planet would have spun up the surface rotation to a rate substantially higher than observed.

paper.title: Multiphase Gas in High-$z$ Cosmic Sheets
paper.abstract: We present high-resolution cosmological simulations of individual cosmic sheets ($z=3-6$) using the moving-mesh code AREPO to study cold gas ($T\approx10^4\rm ~K$) in the diffuse cosmic web. We find cosmic sheet gas forms a fragmented morphology, evident as kiloparsec-scale variations in the neutral hydrogen column density ($N_{\rm HI}$). Fragmentation arises from the bending and disruption of the cold-dense sheet core into a multiphase medium. Nonlinear thin shell instability (NTSI) and later shear-induced vorticity drive this bending, rather than previously suggested thermal or Richtmyer-Meshkov instabilities. Higher resolution enhances fragmentation. Across a fourfold range in spatial resolution, $N_{\rm HI}$ covering fractions increase by factors of $\approx 1.5-3.5$ for partial Lyman-limit systems (pLLS) and Lyman-limit systems (LLS). An order-of-magnitude estimate suggests sheets may host a large fraction of the ultra-low metallicity (p)LLS population. Equivalent MP-Gadget simulations show qualitatively similar fragmentation, but numerical smoothing effects are present. Cosmic-sheet gas properties remain unconverged despite our high resolutions.

paper.title: Sherlock 'Chrones: The Curious Case of NGC 6791 and Asteroseismic Targets Therein Reveals Mixing Length Dependence on Evolutionary Stage
paper.abstract: As single-aged populations containing stars spanning a range of masses but otherwise with similar properties, star clusters provide valuable testbeds for stellar evolution theory. The old, metal-rich, open cluster NGC 6791 is well studied, but the availability of asteroseismic observations of individual cluster members allows for a more in-depth analysis. Driven by mounting evidence that the solar assumption for convection used in almost all 1D stellar models is not adequate, and in light of the increased precision provided by modern data and asteroseismic constraints, we built and compared custom isochrones with varying values of the convective mixing length, $α_\text{MLT}$, to two clusters with well-determined ages: NGC 6791 and the well-studied, metal-poor globular cluster M92. For both clusters, we found that the best-fitting mixing length parameter decreases monotonically as a function of evolutionary phase, finding values between $0.98-1.10α_{\odot}$ for NGC 6791 and $1.16-1.21α_{\odot}$ for M92. In NGC 6791, this corresponds to an 18% decrease in the best fitting mixing length between the main sequence turn-off and upper end of the red giant branch. The degree of variation found within this one object is therefore comparable to variation across the literature in $α_\text{MLT}$ fits for other non-solar targets, calling single-valued $α_\text{MLT}$ fits to clusters into question. It is also consistent with $\log g$-$α_\text{MLT}$ trends predicted by higher-fidelity, 3D convection analyses. Our results therefore illustrate the need for more flexibility in our treatment of the mixing length in isochrones to properly model clusters.

paper.title: 3D Binary Evolution of a Merging Binary Black Hole Progenitor
paper.abstract: Mass transfer is a highly dynamical 3D process that spans evolutionary timescales in binary stars. It is key to the production of gravitational waves through formation of binary black holes and other double compact objects. We integrate global 3D hydrodynamics into stellar evolutionary modeling to resolve mass transfer across nuclear timescales. We employ the shellular approximation in the stellar evolution code MESA to map a 3D spatial structure by equipotential shells in the Roche geometry to maintain hydrostatic equilibrium across tidally-distorted surfaces. We employ the method of time-incremented multiscale evolution to alternate between stellar evolution and 3D hydrodynamics to span large timescales with dynamical feedback. We employ this framework to examine a likely merging binary black hole progenitor system of a low-metallicity 30Msol donor star and 9.3Msol black hole from the end of the main sequence to core Carbon depletion. We modeled two complete mass transfer phases in 3D while self-consistently accounting for stellar evolution. These comprised a thermal-timescale early Case B phase and a nuclear-timescale late Case B phase. The prescription of Kolb & Ritter (1990) closely predicted the results of 3D evolution, except at the end of the first phase of mass transfer; our 3D model remained well-contained by the outer Lagrange point, despite 1D predictions of substantial L3 overflow during this stage. We find incorporating 3D hydrodynamics during Case B mass transfer did not significantly impact expected merger times. Our model never overflowed L3 as predicted by 1D prescriptions. L2/L3 outflows formed even while underflowing those equipotentials. Our model suggests these outflows can be neglected for the evolution of similar systems, but were dense enough to potentially impact X-ray observations.

paper.title: First $Ω_{\rm m}-w$ Measurement Using Only Fast Radio Burst Observations
paper.abstract: Though fast radio bursts (FRBs) are widely advocated as a dark energy probe, no valid $Ω_m-w$ constraint has been obtained exclusively from FRB data to date. Benefiting from a rapidly growing localized sample and a novel statistical framework for modeling the dispersion measure (DM), we report the first simultaneous inference of the matter density $Ω_m$ and dark energy equation of state parameter $w$ from FRBs alone, without external observational priors on these two parameters. We combine a multi-parameter emulator for the nonlinear matter power spectrum with a physically motivated electron prescription to construct a cosmology-dependent cosmic-DM distribution. Within this unified analysis framework, the mean and variance of DM respond self-consistently to the same underlying cosmology, directly connecting the FRB likelihood to both cosmic expansion and structure growth. Analyzing 125 localized FRBs at $0.105\leq z\leq2.148$, we obtain $Ω_m = 0.33^{+0.10}_{-0.11}$ and $w = -0.80^{+0.28}_{-0.38}$ under the flat $w$CDM model. We find a new positive $Ω_m-w$ degeneracy in the FRB posterior, opposite to the strong anticorrelation derived from Type Ia supernovae, offering a complementary test of dark energy properties and highlighting their potential in future precision cosmological studies.

paper.title: FAST Burst-Cluster Catalog of FRB 20240114A
paper.abstract: We present the complete FAST burst-cluster catalog of FRB 20240114A, covering its 495-day active episode from January 28, 2024 to June 5, 2025. The catalog contains 13261 burst clusters, 19037 bursts, and 29026 sub-bursts detected in 99 observing sessions. The data reveal distinct organization across temporal scales. Among drifting burst clusters, downward-drifting clusters outnumber upward-drifting ones by approximately $9.4:1$. Between separate burst clusters, previously reported frequency changes show no preferred direction, while our Weibull analysis finds their arrival times broadly consistent with Poisson statistics, suggesting that burst clusters may represent approximately independent emission episodes within observing sessions. The Parkes/Murriyang observations revealed a long-term modulation of the characteristic emission frequency, and the extended FAST measurements show a consistent evolution. Burst energetics increase with cluster multiplicity and activity level, although significant scatter remains. The manually refined dispersion measure increases at $1.29\pm0.11\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$, enlarging the still limited but growing sample of repeaters with increasing DM. Overall, these results summarize the spectral--temporal evolution of FRB 20240114A and present a burst-cluster catalog linked to the existing BurstID measurements, providing a basis for future studies of repeating FRBs.

paper.title: The Cosmic Infrared Background from Population III.1 Supermassive Stars and Black Holes
paper.abstract: We investigate the cosmic infrared background (CIB) that is expected to arise from the Population (Pop) III.1 supermassive black hole (SMBH) formation scenario, which involves early SMBH seeding via supermassive primordial star formation enabled by dark matter annihilation heating. We model the emission from Pop III.1 supermassive stars, including their growth phase, flash ionization phase, and early black hole accretion phase, as well as accompanying emission from lower-mass Pop III.2 stars. The CIB is composed of stellar and SMBH accretion disk continuum radiation, nebular continuum emission, and Ly$α$ radiation redistributed through scattering in the neutral intergalactic medium. Based on the feedback regulated Pop III.1 model of Petkova et al. (2026), our fiducial model assumes $\sim 10^5\,M_\odot$ Pop III.1 stars forming by $z_{\rm flash}=20$ with a comoving number density of $\sim0.2\,{\rm cMpc}^{-3}$. For this model, the combined stellar contribution is less than $1\%$ of existing direct and diffuse CIB measurements. However, the contribution to the CIB from $z\sim6-20$ SMBH accretion is expected to be larger than the Pop III.1 stellar component for average Eddington ratios $λ_{\text{Edd}} \sim 0.01$. Latest CIB observations place constraints of $λ_{\text{Edd}} \lesssim 0.3$ for the fiducial Pop III.1 model during these epochs.

paper.title: Dark Matter Model Implications of a Candidate Sub-halo Near the Sun, and the Data Needed to Discriminate Among Them
paper.abstract: Pulsar-timing accelerations point to a localized mass concentration near the Sun, consistent with a dark matter sub-halo. We work out what such an object implies for the nature of dark matter, organizing the implications by their observable effect: suppression or enhancement of structure formation, internal structure and survival after formation, and emission or scattering by the constituents. We discuss ultralight wave dark matter, thermal and nonthermal warm dark matter, dark acoustic oscillations and dark matter-baryon scattering, elastic and inelastic self-interactions, invisible decays with recoil, primordial black holes, indirect detection, and a possible connection to the LUX-ZEPLIN high-energy recoil candidate. We then ask what new data would discriminate among these models. The existing accelerations are measured outside the tidal radius, where they are blind to the interior mass distribution, to the object's velocity, and to the sub-halo population. We identify four routes that lift these degeneracies: accelerations measured inside the halo, which separate point-mass, cuspy, and cored profiles; lensing and accretion, which test whether the mass is compact; the morphology of annihilation or decay emission, which probes the inner profile; and a search for a comoving stellar population, which tests whether the object is dark and measures its velocity. We also contrast this program with pulsar-timing-array searches for transiting dark matter substructure, which probe vastly lighter objects through a different observable.

paper.title: A Shallow Phase-resolved Gamma-Ray Luminosity-Cutoff Energy Relation in Globular Cluster Millisecond Pulsars
paper.abstract: Globular clusters (GCs) provide dense stellar environments for investigating the high-energy emission of millisecond pulsars (MSPs). Using $\sim$17.3~yr of \textit{Fermi}-LAT Pass~8 data in the 0.1-500.0~GeV range, we study four MSPs that dominate, or contribute substantially to, the GeV $γ$-ray emission of their host GCs. Significant off-pulse $γ$-ray emission is detected from PSR~J1823$-$3021A, J1824$-$2452A, and J1835$-$3259B. For these sources, the cutoff energy, $E_{\rm cut}$, varies systematically with rotational phase and is positively correlated with the phase-resolved energy flux. Using the phase-resolved isotropic $γ$-ray luminosity ($L_γ$), we find $L_γ\propto E_{\rm cut}^α$ with $α=0.74^{+0.16}_{-0.14}$. This slope is substantially shallower than that reported for field MSPs, $α=2.31^{+0.22}_{-0.25}$, and the $α=16/7\simeq2.29$ scaling expected for curvature radiation in the equatorial current sheet framework. The origin of the shallow relation remains uncertain, potentially reflecting cluster-associated $γ$-ray emission, differences in emission geometry and beaming, or limited photon statistics. Our results demonstrate that GC MSPs provide valuable targets for testing phase-resolved high-energy emission physics in dense stellar environments.

paper.title: The Universality of Halo Growth and Merger Rates in Modified Gravity Theories
paper.abstract: In the standard $Λ$CDM framework, the merger rate of dark matter haloes has been found to follow a nearly universal form, with only weak dependence on halo mass and redshift. We examine whether this universality is preserved in modified gravity (MG) models, where the growth of cosmic structure can deviate from that of general relativity (GR). We use the ELEPHANT suite of large $N$-body simulations to study halo merger rates and mass accretion histories in different modified gravity models, including two representative scenarios beyond-GR: the Hu--Sawicki chameleon $f(R)$ model and the normal branch of the Dvali--Gabadadze--Porrati model. For the mass accretion histories, the modified gravitational effect can produce systematic departures from GR, generally corresponding to more rapid halo growth. The deviations are relatively small when the MG effect is weak, while they become more pronounced in models with strong deviation from GR and can exceed $15\%$ in the extreme case.   For the halo merger rate, we find that the nearly universal behavior is well preserved across all the gravity models, with only weak dependence on redshift and halo mass, reflecting the unbiased accretion nature of halo growth. However, apparent deviation from this universality can arise if the halo mass is not defined consistently with the modified gravity model.

paper.title: Thermodynamic topology and orbital dynamics of charged RN--AdS black hole with logarithmic corrections
paper.abstract: This study investigates the topological thermodynamic properties and orbital dynamics of the Reissner--Nordström anti-de Sitter (RN--AdS) black hole with logarithmic corrections solution in Einstein--Maxwell gravity. By utilizing the Duan's $Φ$-mapping theory, we investigate the topological classes within the generalized three-parameter Sharma--Mittal entropy formalism. Employing different thermodynamic ensembles, including the canonical and mixed canonical ensembles, we explore the critical, divergence points and heat capacity, which help us determine the thermodynamic stability of the BH. In addition, the Hamiltonian formalism is employed to investigate the orbital and oscillatory motion of neutral test particles. By utilizing the effective potential approach, we examine the effective force, the stability of circular orbits, and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO). We further analyze the trajectories of test particles and derive the radial $\left(ω_{r}\right)$, latitudinal $\left(ω_θ\right)$, and azimuthal $\left(ω_φ\right)$ oscillation frequencies, together with the periastron precession frequency. paper.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients with high brightness temperatures, but their physical origin remains uncertain. The search yields apparent period candidates with nominal Poisson-calibrated significances comparable to that reported for the 1.7 s signal, although the inferred periods vary substantially among sources and observing windows. We then perform a nonparametric waiting-time randomization test, in which the observed waiting-time distribution is preserved while the temporal ordering is destroyed. The randomized sequences reproduce the main candidate-period structures seen in the data, demonstrating that these apparent periodicities can arise from the non-Poissonian waiting-time statistics rather than from a coherent periodic process. Rotation-modulated epidemic-type aftershock sequence simulations provide a complementary parametric illustration of the same effect. We therefore find no robust evidence for a short intrinsic periodicity in these data, and the reported 1.7 s signal is not uniquely distinguished from clustering-induced candidates. Robust periodicity searches must evaluate significance against null models that account for the observed waiting-time statistics and the full search procedure.

paper.abstract: We develop a simple analytic two-component model that links the thermal evolution of self-gravitating systems to black-hole thermodynamics. We then contrast this behavior with Schwarzschild anti-de Sitter black holes. Despite the disparate microphysics, both systems exhibit a switch in heat-capacity behavior governed by competing pressure contributions. The surrogate model provides compact analytic insight into stability thresholds in self-gravitating systems and their black-hole analogues.

paper.title: Hard X-ray flux rope anchor points in the October 2024 X9 flare
paper.abstract: In recent studies, signatures of non-thermal hard X-ray (HXR) emission at the anchor point of erupting flux ropes were reported, suggesting that accelerated electrons trapped in the erupting flux ropes can reach the chromosphere and produce Bremsstrahlung emission there. We investigated the HXR sources observed during the impulsive phase of the X9-class flare SOL2024-10-03T12:18 from AR 13842 and assessed whether any of the HXR sources are associated with the anchor points of the erupting flux rope. We analysed the evolution and location of the flare ribbon sources and coronal dimmings to diagnose the eruption process by using multi-vantage point data from the Solar Orbiter and Earth-orbiting instruments. We combined this with a pre-eruption non-linear force-free magnetic field extrapolation to reconstruct the initial magnetic connectivity and compare it to the observed flare ribbons and dimming locations. The magnetic field extrapolation shows two flux ropes before the flare onset. Tether-cutting reconnection during the impulsive phase of the flare results in a larger erupting flux rope formed by the reconnection of the two pre-existing flux ropes. The Spectrometer/Telescope for Imaging X-rays on Solar Orbiter observes at least four distinct HXR sources: two flare footpoints and two additional outer sources at the anchor points of the erupting flux rope. These observations corroborate earlier speculations that non-thermal electrons trapped in the erupting flux rope precipitate along the field lines into the denser chromosphere.

paper.title: Direct simulation Monte Carlo for dark matter production and phase-space evolution
paper.abstract: To study the early-universe production of dark matter particles beyond thermal equilibrium often requires solving several coupled Boltzmann equations at the phase-space level. We present a new method to address this challenge using Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) based on stochastic interactions of an ensemble of particles. We implement and validate efficient algorithms to describe freeze-out, decays, elastic scattering and number-changing processes within the dark sector. These algorithms do not require a discretisation of momentum space on a pre-defined grid and do not rely on approximations such as thermally averaged cross sections. As illustrative example, we consider a scenario with two-step dark matter production, leading to a bimodal phase-space distribution, and consider the subsequent evolution under elastic and number-changing processes. We show that DSMC is a flexible approach to explore out-of-equilibrium processes and solve Boltzmann equations at the phase-space level in order to predict the abundance of dark matter particles and their effect on structure formation.

paper.title: Square Kilometre Array Science Data Challenge 3b: EoR inference
paper.abstract: We present and analyse the results of Science Data Challenge 3b (SDC3b; https://sdc3.skao.int/challenges/inference), an Epoch of Reionization (EoR) inference exercise organised by the Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKAO) using simulated SKA data. The nine-month challenge, running from October 2024 to May 2025, represents the first community-wide comparison of EoR inference pipelines on common simulated datasets. We consider multiple datasets designed to assess performance on both foreground-free and foreground-contaminated cylindrical power spectra and imaging products, adopting different reionization scenarios and EoR simulation models. We include results from 16 teams, which employ a range of methodologies to infer the posterior distribution of the hydrogen neutral fraction across three redshift intervals spanning z=8.41 to z=6.25. The results show significant inter-team variability of the astrophysical constraints even in the simpler case where only instrumental noise is added to the cosmological signal. This underscores the need for further investigation into the relative contributions of signal modelling, the treatment of instrumental effects, and inference methods to the robustness of the resulting conclusions. Although individual methods can produce biased parameter estimates, the combined average of their estimates remains close to the input values, suggesting that independent approaches can offset method-specific biases.

paper.title: Resonant Cavity Searches for Millicharged Dark Matter
paper.abstract: A plethora of resonant cavity experiments have been designed to search for ultralight dark matter (DM) candidates, such as axion or dark-photon DM. In this work, we show that these same apparatuses can be sensitive to ultralight millicharged dark matter (mDM) with masses $m_φ\sim1-100\,μ\mathrm{eV}$. Similar to axion DM, in the presence of a background magnetic field, mDM acts as an effective current which can excite the modes of a resonant cavity. Importantly, for a cylindrical cavity, axion DM dominantly couples to the transverse magnetic (TM) modes, whereas mDM dominantly couples to the transverse electric (TE) modes. We project the sensitivity to mDM that resonant cavity experiments can achieve if they are able to tune and readout their TE modes. We find that fractional millicharges as small as $ε_m=e_m/e\sim10^{-19}$ can be probed. If mDM constitutes only a subfraction $f_\mDM \lesssim0.2\%$ of the total DM density, competing astrophysical bounds do not apply. In this case, resonant cavities can be the most sensitive probes of mDM in this mass range.

paper.title: The origin of the apparent ULX deficit in NGC 3256
paper.abstract: Ultra-luminous X-ray (ULX) sources are bright, off-nuclear X-ray point sources, mostly associated with high-mass X-ray binaries (HMXBs), with a compact object accreting from a donor star at super-Eddington luminosities. Although their HMXB nature implies a connection to star formation processes, previous works have found that luminous infrared galaxies (LIRGs) appear to have a deficit of ULXs compared to their very high star formation rates (SFRs). Here, we analyze three Chandra observations of NGC 3256, a merging LIRG with SFR ~50-60 Msun/yr. Based on local scaling relations, it could be expected to host between 100-120 individual ULXs, which could have a non-negligible impact on the energetics and feedback processes of the galaxy. We aim to characterize all its detected X-ray point sources to determine if there is a ULX deficit in this galaxy. We also aim to explore the potential impact of host-galaxy obscuration and metallicity in said deficit. We characterize the luminosity of each X-ray point source in each Chandra observation, and use all observations to determine their potential ULX nature and the fraction of transient ULXs, as well as construct a ULX luminosity function for this galaxy. We find that the galaxy hosts 10-15 ULXs, making it one of the most ULX-rich galaxies known to date. While comparison with the ULX/SFR ratio of nearby galaxies predicted as many as ~100 ULXs, we show that, when accounting for its very high metallicity, NGC 3256 does not have a ULX deficit; and may even present an excess. While the high obscuration in LIRGs has previously been invoked to explain the ULX deficit, we conclude that it is not required to explain the ULX to SFR ratio in NGC 3256. If obscuration still plays a role, then LIRGs may actually be significantly more efficient at producing ULXs than normal galaxies (of the same metallicity), in disagreement with previous results.

paper.title: Neutral hydrogen in the Shapley Supercluster core II. Gas content and star formation in the filaments connecting the core
paper.abstract: We investigate the neutral atomic hydrogen (HI) content of galaxies across the Shapley Supercluster (SSC) at z = 0.048 by combining new deep MeerKAT L band observations of five filament pointings with archival MeerKAT Galaxy Cluster Legacy Survey observations of the supercluster core. Together with optical data from the Shapley Supercluster Survey, these observations provide a homogeneous view of galaxy evolution from the virialised cluster environment to the surrounding filaments. We compare the HI content, star formation activity, gas depletion timescales, and morphological properties of galaxies relative to the gas fraction and star forming main sequences. The global HI detection fraction increases from 30 per cent in the cluster centre to 45 per cent in the filaments. While HI detected galaxies in the cluster centre are dominated by transition zone systems, the filament population is shared nearly equally between star forming main sequence and transition zone detections, indicating ongoing environmental transformation. Their gas properties also differ: cluster galaxies exhibit progressively depleted HI reservoirs towards the red sequence, whereas filament galaxies remain primarily gas rich. Within the filaments, long HI depletion timescales exceeding the Hubble time are concentrated in specific populations, notably 71 per cent of transition zone and 57 per cent of gas rich detections, indicating the inefficient conversion of atomic gas into stars. The HI detected filament population is dominated by late type galaxies, while the underlying non detected population is primarily composed of early type systems, consistent with environmental pre processing before cluster infall.

paper.title: Gamma-Ray Bursts from Primordial Black Hole-Induced Neutron Star Collapse
paper.abstract: We show that the capture and subsequent endoparasitic consumption of a neutron star (NS) by a primordial black hole (PBH) can produce a short gamma-ray burst (GRB) without forming an accretion disk. During PBH-induced NS consumption, the NS spin is amplified through angular-momentum conservation and transfer from infalling matter, while flux freezing and a differential-rotation-driven dynamo amplify the magnetic field. We find that, for rapidly rotating millisecond pulsars (MSPs), these mechanisms can power short GRBs through magnetic dipole radiation and magnetic energy release. If asteroid-mass PBHs in the range $10^{-14}M_\odot$--$10^{-11}M_\odot$ constitute the dark matter, we estimate that searches of the Fermi-GBM archive and a future MeV gamma-ray mission such as COSI could detect these bursts. We also discuss possible multimessenger counterparts, including fast radio bursts powered by magnetic energy release, kilonovae and $511\,{\rm keV}$ line emission associated with centrifugally ejected neutron-rich matter, and gravitational waves from the rapid collapse and subsequent black-hole ringdown. Together, these signals probe complementary stages of PBH-induced NS consumption.

paper.title: Mauve Observations of the Eclipsing Binary System $β$ Lyrae
paper.abstract: We present a broadband, synoptic observing campaign of the complex eclipsing binary system $β$ Lyr, obtained with the first commercial astronomical satellite, Mauve, developed and operated by Blue Skies Space Ltd. Mauve's capabilities have resulted in the first multiphase monitoring of $β$ Lyr, covering UV and optical photometry, as well as low-resolution spectrophotometry, including the phase-folded mapping of the intensity of a number of emission lines. The different components in its spectrum vary in very different ways, indicative of a system with a number of physical components. Our data show that while most of the components show repeatable cycle-to-cycle variability, the thus far hardly observed UV emission (2000-3000 Angstrom) varies significantly from one cycle to the other, pointing to the need for simultaneous observations to understand and model the system. These observations reveal that the ultraviolet-emitting structures in this benchmark interacting binary evolve on timescales of individual orbits, challenging the assumption of a stationary accretion geometry commonly adopted in models of interacting binary stars. The quality of the data set and the fresh view that they bring to a well studied, but still poorly understood object demonstrate the scientific value of small telescopes with focused scientific capabilities, as well as the value of a new generation of commercial astronomical instrumentation.

paper.title: Spatio-Temporal Evolution of a Steady Transition Region Downflow above a Sunspot
paper.abstract: Super-Sonic Downflows (SSDs) are usually observed above sunspots as redshifted peaks in lower Transition Region (TR) spectral lines and can last from a few minutes to several hours. Utilising high-cadence, $\sim$3 hour long repeated-raster mode observations from Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS), we investigate the spatio-temporal dynamics of such a downflow event above NOAA active region 12135. Triple Gaussian fitting to TR spectral lines, along with Non-Force Free Field (NFFF) extrapolation and Differential Emission Measure (DEM) analysis, is performed to study this event. Downflow is initially observed in both the umbral and penumbral regions. Over time, the penumbral downflow fades, while the umbral downflow strengthens and appears as a single structure initially but eventually splits into two spatial segments. The calculated average properties, including downflow speed, electron density, and mass flux for this event, align with established studies. Simultaneous evolution in overlying coronal loops is also observed using imaging data from the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA). DEM analysis of the coronal emission over the downflow region indicates corresponding changes in cool ($\log_{10}[T/\mathrm{K}] \in [5.5, 5.6]$) coronal plasma. As suggested by recurrent transient brightenings observed in the nearby region in coronal channels and the corresponding fan-spine magnetic topology identified from NFFF extrapolations, magnetic reconnection occurring in this region is proposed to be the cause of this evolution. Our analysis revealed that changes in the morphology of TR downflows are closely associated with evolution of overlying coronal loops.

paper.title: Revisiting Kerr-Newman-(A)dS Black Holes in \(f(R)\) Gravity: A Kerr-Schild Approach
paper.abstract: It is known that, in the constant-curvature regime, the field equations of $f(R)$ gravity reduce to the Einstein form with an effective cosmological constant, establishing a direct correspondence between stationary and axisymmetric black hole solutions in $f(R)$ gravity and their counterparts in general relativity, including the Kerr--Newman--(A)dS family. Within this framework, we revisit the derivation of these metrics using the Kerr--Schild approach for illustrative purposes. The Maxwell equations are solved independently of the Kerr--Schild function, allowing the electromagnetic source to be determined before addressing the gravitational field equations. We then investigate the possibility of non-constant-curvature solutions, taking quadratic $f(R)$ gravity as a representative model. Remarkably, the field equations within the Kerr--Schild ansatz force the Ricci scalar to be constant, reducing the resulting geometries to the familiar Kerr--Newman--(A)dS family. Thus, our analysis extends the recently established no-go result for uncharged black holes to electrically charged configurations within the framework considered here.

paper.title: Worldsheet Effective Theory of Abelian-Higgs Cosmic Strings beyond Nambu--Goto
paper.abstract: Cosmic strings can support long-lived excitations confined to their cores, opening channels for energy exchange with the transverse Goldstone modes that describe the string's motion. We derive a covariant worldsheet theory of their coupled dynamics directly from the Abelian-Higgs model at critical coupling, with all interaction coefficients fixed by the microscopic theory. The resulting action, which we validate against numerical lattice field theory simulations, extends the Nambu--Goto description to include a massive scalar shape mode and a massive vector mode. Dualizing the vector reveals a geometric distinction: the shape scalar mode couples to intrinsic worldsheet curvature, while the pseudoscalar couples to normal bundle curvature. These interactions explain the distinct parametric instabilities observed in lattice simulations and predict how the relative polarization of colliding transverse waves controls the excitation of the two internal modes. Our results connect microscopic string structure to the nonlinear worldsheet dynamics, providing a predictive framework for cosmic strings beyond the Nambu--Goto approximation.

paper.title: Strong Field Tidal Disruptions of Rotating Stars by Spinning Black Holes
paper.abstract: We study tidal disruptions of rotating solar-type stars by a rapidly spinning supermassive black hole with general-relativistic smoothed-particle hydrodynamics. To capture strong-field effects, we place the pericentre at a few gravitational radii of a black hole, and compare with weak-field encounters at a larger pericentre around a lighter black hole. We vary the black hole spin, the orbital inclination and the stellar rotation, using rigidly and differentially rotating stars with spin aligned, anti-aligned or perpendicular to the orbital angular momentum. In the strong field, the black hole spin decides whether a core survives on equatorial and inclined orbits, and stellar rotation reduces the surviving core in every partial disruption. At the larger pericentre, as in Newtonian studies, anti-aligned rotation instead protects the star from disruption. In both cases the tide reverses an anti-aligned spin just before pericentre. The outcome differs because in the strong field the tide keeps acting on the reversed core long after pericentre. Deep encounters leave cores spinning above break-up, which shed mass and angular momentum as they settle. Full disruptions approach the canonical fallback law, whereas the late-time slope of partial disruptions is not universal and is set by the debris energy distribution near the surviving core.

paper.title: SlotFlow-GB: A Neural Framework for Trans-Dimensional Inference of Overlapping Galactic Binaries
paper.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe the millihertz gravitational-wave sky, including millions of long-lived Galactic binaries (GBs), tens of thousands of which are expected to be individually resolvable throughout the mission's lifetime. Extracting these sources requires jointly determining their number and physical parameters from strongly overlapping signals, posing a computationally demanding trans-dimensional inference problem. We introduce SlotFlow-GB, a neural framework that constructs a learned approximation to the trans-dimensional posterior, producing a probability distribution over source multiplicity and parameter densities for individual binaries in a single evaluation, without requiring their number to be specified in advance. We demonstrate this framework using year-long LISA simulations containing up to ten binaries within a 2 $μ$Hz frequency interval, focusing on a high-SNR regime in which source overlap, rather than individual-source detectability, is the primary challenge. The inferred source count differs from the true count by at most one in 94% of cases, while the model identifies individual binaries even when their signals overlap strongly in frequency. A complete evaluation, including parameter sampling, takes just 41 ms per band on one NVIDIA GH200 GPU, or 530 ms on eight laptop CPU threads. We further demonstrate that these distributions can be used to initialize subsequent likelihood-based inference, connecting fast amortized predictions with joint parameter estimation.

paper.title: Galaxy Bias and Soft Limits from Inflation
paper.abstract: Primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG) leaves an imprint on large-scale structure through a scale-dependent galaxy bias, and properly incorporating the effects of higher order PNG into the bias expansion requires a consistent renormalization framework that extends beyond the squeezed limit of the bispectrum. We develop the multi-loop renormalization of bias operators in the presence of non-vanishing primordial n-point functions of arbitrary order, including stochastic contributions. We show that galaxy bias renormalization is determined by the multi-soft limits of primordial correlators and bias kernels. We provide explicit computations for one- and two-loop renormalization of deterministic operators up to fifth order in the bias expansion. Finally, we derive the renormalization group equations for the bias parameters at one and two loops.

paper.title: Periodicities of small regular jet deviations in SS433 and their origin
paper.abstract: Based on the results of spectroscopic observations of SS433 conducted with the 2.5-m telescope at the Caucasian Mountain Observatory between 2020 and 2026, we study the deviations of the moving hydrogen and helium emission lines from their positions as predicted by the kinematic model of the jets' precessional motion. In these deviations, in addition to the previously known periodicities of $13^d.08$, $11^d.27$, $6^d.29$, and $5^d.83$, a new period of $3^d.08$ is identified. All observed periodicities are explained by a model in which the jet offsets occur in a fixed direction relative to the star-disk axis $\bf r$, and the magnitude of the offset is a function $a(μ)$, where $μ$ is the cosine of the angle between $\bf r$ and the direction of each jet. The odd terms of the power series expansion of $a(μ)$ in $μ$ yield periodicities of $6^d.29$, $5^d.83$, and $3^d.08$, with the jets shifting in opposite directions while remaining parallel. The even powers yield periodicities of $13^d.08$, $11^d.27$, and $4^d.14$ (the latter is not observed), with both jets shifting in the same direction, which was previously misinterpreted as a change in the jets' total velocity $β$. With the exception of the $6^d.29$ periodicity, all other displacements occur at an angle of $\approx120^\circ$ to $\bf r$. Superimposed on the regular variability are random deviations (jitter) in the jet directions, independent for the two jets, with $σ\lesssim1.\!\!^\circ5$.

paper.title: Log-periodic radiation cores and light rings in pure quadratic bulk gravity
paper.abstract: In the pure quadratic model of the Böhmer--Jensko bulk--boundary formulation of gravity, every static metric with a regular centre has vanishing central density and pressure, so no affine equation of state admits a regular non-vacuum star. We therefore study singular cores, in scale-invariant variables in which the isotropy condition is a single autonomous relation between two functions. Closures that keep the self-similar solutions as equilibria fix the stability of two vacuum lines but leave that of the matter-bearing equilibria undetermined, except at one unphysical point, so only an equation of state yields definite dynamics. For a linear equation of state the closed system has a focus, a saddle, and a vacuum point with nonzero bulk scalar that exchanges stability with the saddle in a transcritical bifurcation. At the radiation value the system is integrable, through the Tolman integral and scale invariance, and the focus becomes a nonlinear centre surrounded by log-periodic solutions. Radiation is also exactly where the line containing the matter-bearing equilibria of this closure coincides with the line of circular null orbits. Consequently every periodic radiation core with monotonic areal radius has exactly one stable and one unstable light ring per period, at radii forming two interlaced geometric progressions towards the centre with a common ratio tending to 2.165 for small oscillations. In the optical geometry the self-similar solution is a cylinder and each core a periodic tube, whose bulges and necks carry these rings. MIT bag-model configurations whose cores approach these orbits inherit this structure.

paper.title: Cardinal RG=GR: Phase-Space Cardinality and the Cosmological Constant and Hierarchy Problems
paper.abstract: The effective field theory approach constructs the low-energy theory by integrating out fluctuations above an ultraviolet scale which raises the cosmological constant and hierarchy problems. We investigate an alternative prescription in which the quantum theory is restricted to a finite accessible region of phase space, characterized by a dimensionless cardinality $\mathcal N$, rather than by independently prescribed spacetime and momentum scales. At fixed cardinality these scales are related. For Euclidean de Sitter space, the stationarity condition for the gravitational action can then be written as a stationarity condition with respect to the momentum scale, a relation which we call Cardinal RG=GR. We demonstrate the relation between $\mathcal N$ and the Gibbons-Hawking entropy of de Sitter space, compute the cosmological constant proportional to ${1}/{\sqrt{\mathcal N}}$, show that it is radiatively stable and apply the same prescription to demonstrate the radiative stability of the mass parameter for a simple interacting scalar field model, thereby illuminating the resolution of the hierarchy problem. We also establish a precise limit, involving gravitational data, in which the conventional results of Quantum Field Theory and the Renormalization Group are recovered.

paper.title: Connecting Coronal Loop Scaling Laws and Kink Wave Heating: An Analytical and Numerical Study
paper.abstract: Turbulent dissipation of kink waves has been proposed as one of the mechanisms responsible for the observed high coronal temperatures. We test this hypothesis by examining the effect of this heating mechanism on coronal loops. The coronal loop static and dynamic behaviour is investigated under the assumption that the heating in the loop is primarily provided by kink wave dissipation. The heating term is borrowed from the recently developed UAWSoM model. Loop modelling is done in 1D using three different methods: one analytical following the principles first set in the RTV scaling laws, and two numerical: one based on the setup used to derive the RTVS scaling laws, and UAWSoM. We provide scaling laws and estimate density, temperature, and pressure, as well as kink wave heating rate and kink wave energy density needed to counteract energy loss by thermal conduction and radiative cooling. Estimates of kink wave energy density needed to heat the loop to 1 MK correspond to maximum velocity amplitudes of around 35 km s$^{-1}$ near the loop apex. Loop radius, density contrast and filling factor are found to affect the predictions significantly. The two numerical methods agree to a high degree. The analytical method predicts that $W_\textrm{k} \propto PL^{-2/3}$, while the two numerical methods show a wider range of scaling exponents which depend on the location in the loop. UAWSoM simulations suggest that loops may exhibit dynamic behaviour for a wide range of loop conditions, which may include thermal non-equilibrium cycles and periods of emerging and dissipating slow waves. Overall, estimates of kink wave energy density and scaling laws provide observational constraints on the importance of the proposed kink wave heating mechanism, with the current preliminary results suggesting that the uniturbulent kink wave heating may be a significant source of energy and heat in coronal loops.

paper.abstract: On 2025 November 12, the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) network detected S251112cm, a compact binary merger candidate with a false alarm rate of one per four years at a luminosity distance of $93 \pm 27$ Mpc. The probability that the lighter component's mass lies below 1 $M_\odot$ is >99%, while the probability that either component lies at 1-3 $M_\odot$ is only 8%, leaving the nature of the progenitor system unclear. We present Pan-STARRS and ATLAS optical follow-up of the 90% localisation region, and quantify Vera C. Rubin Observatory target-of-opportunity observations. In the North, Pan-STARRS imaged 1084 deg$^2$ (65%) within 7 days to a median depth of 21.9 mag and ATLAS 1545 deg$^2$ (87%) within 14 days to 19.3 mag across both hemispheres; in the South, Rubin covered 849 deg$^2$ (36%) 2-10 days post-merger to median depths of 24.5 ($g$) and 23.5 ($i$) mag. They reported 173, 93 and 67 candidates respectively (269 unique), which we assess against AT 2017gfo-like kilonova and SN 1998bw-like broad-lined Type Ic supernova models using prior activity, host luminosity distance, photometric evolution and absolute magnitude. Eight survive, mainly for lack of distance information. Six of these lie in hosts fainter than any in a volume-limited comparison sample, suggesting they are background sources. AT 2025aimy declines too slowly for the AT 2017gfo-like model, and a VLT host spectrum places AT 2025alqe outside the LVK volume, leaving no convincing counterpart candidates. Pan-STARRS and Rubin together exclude both models in $\sim$80% of the 90% localisation volume: the deepest wide-area constraint on a subsolar-mass merger to date and, to our knowledge, the most complete optical coverage of a significant subsolar-mass candidate.

paper.title: Sourcing vector perturbations in warm inflation through shear viscous effects
paper.abstract: Vector modes are generally believed not to play a significant role in standard cosmological perturbation theory because they decay rapidly. Non-equilibrium dynamics in the radiation bath present during warm inflation can lead to shear viscous effects, requiring a description beyond the perfect-fluid approximation. We adopt the fluctuating hydrodynamic approach to account for stochastic anisotropic stress related to shear viscosity. We show that the vector mode obeys a constrained Langevin equation in an inflationary background. The resulting power spectrum, considered in the weak-viscosity regime, is proportional to the shear viscosity and it also depends on the Hubble slow-roll parameter $ε$, decaying approximately as $a^{-(1-ε)}$. This behaviour is significantly slower than the unsourced, non-viscous power spectrum, which decays as $a^{-4}$. The continuously sourced vector modes, nevertheless, decay on superhorizon scales, and the illustrative benchmark parameter choices adopted in our numerical examples give a negligible late-time vector-to-scalar ratio. Despite the absence of direct large-scale observable vector signatures, the main results establish a source of vector perturbations during warm inflation and provide a framework for studying possible secondary effects along with large-scale white noises in the vector channel.

paper.title: Two powers, one scalar field: unified early and late dark energy
paper.abstract: We investigate whether a single canonical scalar field can account for both early and late dark energy. We consider a double-power potential in which a steep positive-power term can generate an early peak in the scalar energy-density fraction, while an inverse-power term supports late-time acceleration. This evolution requires the steep term to dominate initially and become subdominant later. We test the model against cosmic microwave background (CMB) measurements, Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) baryon acoustic oscillations, and Pantheon+ supernova data, with the SH0ES host-distance calibration. Relative to flat $Λ$CDM, the data fit improves by $Δχ^2_{\rm data}=-6.90$, or $Δχ^2_{\rm objective}=-3.76$ when Gaussian parameter-prior penalties are included. The scalar-field model gives $H_0=69.53\pm0.26\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, compared with $68.45\pm0.24\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ in flat $Λ$CDM. This shift brings the inferred expansion rate closer to the SH0ES measurement, but does not resolve the discrepancy significantly.
